sentences.text: The 3rd respondent in the OP is the appellant in MACA. No.544 of 2015.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioners are the widow and minor children of deceased by name Pramod Kumar, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.12.2011.

According to the petitioners, when the deceased was riding a motor cycle KL-04-5396 from Poozhikkadu to Pandalam through MC road, a tipper lorry, bearing registration No. KL- 29B-5566 driven by the 1st respondent dashed against the motor cycle and as a result of which he fell down and sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries, on the very same day.
3. The 2nd respondent is the owner, the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A11.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
5. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal Awarded a compensation of Rs.14,66,000/-.
Aggrieved by above Award, 3rd respondent preferred MACA. 544 of 2015 and petitioners preferred MACA No.793 of 2015.

6. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

7. Heard Sri. Mathews Jacob, the learned Senior Standing Counsel appearing for the appellant/insurance Company in MACA 544/2015 and Sri.A.N. Santhosh, learned Counsel for the petitioners/ appellant in MACA.793/2015.
8.
The Point: At the time of arguments, negligence on the part of the 1st respondent and the liability of the 3 rd respondent were not disputed.

The learned Senior Counsel, who was appearing for the 3 rd MACA. Nos.544/2015 &793/2015 2025:KER:5509 respondent mainly contended that, towards future prospects, the Tribunal has added 50% of the income, which is against the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].
9.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of the incident, the deceased was aged 30 years.
He was an Electrician cum Plumber.
In the claim petition the petitioners would contend that the deceased was having a monthly income of Rs.20,000/-.
The Tribunal fixed his notional income at Rs.6,000/-.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the notional income of a Coolie during the year 2011 will come to Rs.8,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner being an Electrician cum Plumber, I hold that his notional income is to be fixed little above that of a Coolie and accordingly, the notional income of the deceased is fixed at Rs9,000/-.

the light of the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 17.
11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the deceased has two dependents, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted towards personal and living expenses, in the light of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.17,13,600/-
12.
The learned Senior Counsel would argue that towards funeral expenses, Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-.
Towards loss of consortium and Love and affection, a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- was awarded, which are against the dictum laid down in the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra).

It is true that as per the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra) the petitioners can claim only a sum of Rs.15,000/-
each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium,
with an increase of 10% for every three years.
Therefore, the amount of compensation on account of loss of estate and funeral expense will come to Rs.18,150/- each and Rs.48,400 each towards loss of consortium.
Therefore, the excess amount awarded by the Tribunal on those heads are to be reduced accordingly.
14. The learned counsel for the petitioners would argue that the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering and hence it is to be enhanced.
It is true that the deceased died on the date of accident itself.

Even then, in the light of Kerala Torts (Miscellaneous Provisions)
Act, 1977 the legal representatives are entitled to claim compensation under the head pain and suffering.(see Jaya v. Shaji, AIR 2014 Ker.19 and The Oriental Insurance Co. and Others v.
Vijayamma and Others, 2023 (6) KLT 469).

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co. and Others v.
Vijayamma and Others, 2023 (6) KLT 469)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, I am inclined to award a compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering.
15. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

16. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.18,73,700/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:
MACA. Nos.544/2015 &793/2015 2025:KER:5509 Sl.

Head of claim Amount awarded by The amount given No. the Tribunal (Rs) in appeal (Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 12,24,000/- 17,13,600/- 2 Pain and sufferings 10,000/- 25,000/- 3 Funeral Expenses 25,000/- 18,150/- 4 Transport to hospital 1,000/- 1,000/- 5 Damage to clothes 1,000/- 1,000/- 6 Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/- Nil 7 Loss of consortium 1,00,000/- 96,800/-(48400x2) 8 Loss of estate 5,000/- 18,150/-
Total 14,66,000/- 18,73,700/-

4

In the result, these Appeals are allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.18,73,700/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs Seventy Three Thousand and Seven Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till realisation, excluding interest for a period of 194 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, MACA. Nos.544/2015 &793/2015 2025:KER:5509 excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay and as per rules.

Sd/-
